en.headline: Banks probe unauthorised iPhone pre-order charges on credit cards
en.dek: HSBC, Hang Seng and Standard Chartered are investigating reports of unauthorised Apple Store transactions after iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders opened on Saturday evening.
body: Several banks including HSBC, Hang Seng Bank and Standard Chartered said they are investigating reports of unauthorised credit-card transactions linked to Apple’s online store after pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max opened at 8pm on Saturday.

Social-media users reported receiving charge alerts for amounts matching phone prices, some claiming multiple transactions or totals exceeding HK$60,000, even when they had not completed an order. Banks advised customers to freeze cards via apps or phone if suspicious activity appears and to report promptly to the bank and police.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority noted that merchants may choose not to apply extra authentication such as 3-D Secure for operational reasons, in which case the merchant bears responsibility for unauthorised transactions. Banks said they would support affected customers and initiate chargeback procedures where applicable if the transactions are confirmed as unauthorised.

zh.headline: 多銀行調查iPhone預購未授權信用卡交易
zh.dek: 滙豐、恒生及渣打表示正調查iPhone 18 Pro預購開放後出現的未授權Apple交易報告。
body: 滙豐、恒生銀行及渣打等多家銀行表示，正調查社交平台出現的未授權信用卡交易報告。有關交易涉及Apple網上商店，發生在周六晚上8時iPhone 18 Pro及Pro Max預購開放之後。
多名網民表示收到與手機售價相符的扣款通知，部分人指有多筆交易或累計金額超過6萬元，即使未成功下單。銀行提醒客戶如發現可疑交易，應立即透過手機應用程式凍結信用卡或致電銀行，並向銀行及警方報案。
金管局指出，個別商戶可能基於營運考慮而不使用額外認證安排，在此情況下商戶須承擔非授權交易的責任及財務損失。銀行表示會支援受影響客戶，並在適用情況下根據信用卡組織規則啟動退單機制。
